title: Inquest into police custody death resumes
article: Two Niagara Regional Police officers testified Thursday during an inquest into the death of a man who died while in police custody in Niagara Falls.
Constables Christopher Vassallo and Barry Ravenek took the stand and recounted what they experienced on Bender Hill on July 25, 2007.

The inquest resumed this week, after inquest coroner Dr. David Eden adjourned the matter in April due to a possible conflict of interest between a witness and one of the officers involved in the incident.
The inquest in St. Catharines is looking into circumstances surrounding Orlando Rotolo's death in July 2007.

A 29-year-old Oakville resident, Rotolo died of acute cocaine toxicity at Greater Niagara General Hospital following an altercation with six Niagara Regional Police officers on Bender Hill near Victoria Ave.
Ravenek testified he and Vassallo were on duty in a marked police car when they were alerted to an incident in the Bender Hill area around 5:30 a.m.
He said as he was driving up Bender St. toward Ontario Ave. he saw a male, who he described as "heavy set" and approximately 300 pounds.
"I noted as he was running he was ... turning his head left and right, almost giving the impression he was being chased or chasing," said Ravenek.
Ravenek told the jury he activated the police car's emergency light and hit the siren once. He stopped the vehicle and told Rotolo to stop.

Ravenek said he told Rotolo to put his hands on the squad car. He said Rotolo paused and then did so. Ravenek said he asked him, "What's going on?" Ravenek said he stepped closer to Rotolo, who said nothing.
"He took his hands off the car and lunged directly towards me," said Ravenek.
Ravenek said Vassallo, who was out of the police car, wrapped his arms around Rotolo.
Ravenek said by this time, another police officer became involved and the three officers tried to apprehend Rotolo.
" We told him to stop resisting. He did not comply. He demonstrated, to me, assaultive behaviour."
Ravenek said Vassallo and another officer managed to get Rotolo down.
"I decided to draw my baton while he was on the ground and I delivered one baton strike," said Ravenek. He said he intended to hit Rotolo in his right thigh, but it struck his shin area instead.
During the altercation, Ravenek said he again told Rotolo to stop resisting, to lay down."
Ravenek said Rotolo persisted, again overpowering police, so he delivered a second baton strike, this time hitting his right thigh.
Like the first strike, Ravenek said the baton effort was unsuccessful.
He said Rotolo ran toward the entrance to the casino. He said the man jumped down a retaining wall to a parking lot.
"I watched him jump," said Ravenek, describing it as a "nosedive."
"He hit the pavement with his head."

Ravenek said officers ran toward where Rotolo was. The officer said he noticed a large amount of blood coming from the man's head. He said he asked Rotolo to put his hands behind his back. Unsuccessfully trying to arrest him, the officer said he delivered a knee strike to Rotolo's mid-section, which he said didn't elicit a reaction.
"I then delivered two more."
